Mightily
MY-ti-lee
adv.
From mighty, Saxon mihtig, and the adverbial -ly. Webster 1828: with great power, force, or vehemence; with strength. Scripture uses it of the Spirit falling on a man, of the word of God spreading, of a city crying to God, and of God working in a labouring apostle.

Biblical Definition

Mightily in Scripture describes power at work, and its subject is almost always God. Luke summarises the whole Ephesian ministry — the burned books, the failed exorcists, the riot of the silversmiths — in seven words: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed (Acts 19:20). The word grows; the word prevails; the men are instruments. The same adverb marks the Spirit’s descent on Samson: the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand (Judges 14:6). Note the sequence Scripture insists on: the strength was the Spirit’s, not the man’s, and it came upon a man whose private life was already compromised. Paul describes his own labour the same way, refusing to separate his effort from God’s working: Whereunto I also labour, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily (Colossians 1:29) — genuine striving, genuinely his, and the energy in it God’s. And the king of Nineveh commands the word of a repenting city: let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way (Jonah 3:8).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 defines MIGHTILY as with great power, force, or strength; vigorously; powerfully; with great earnestness or vehemence; and, in a secondary sense, greatly or to a great degree.

expand to see more

MIGHTILY, adv. — With great power, force, or strength; vigorously; powerfully.

Vehemently; with great earnestness; as, to cry mightily unto God.

Greatly; to a great degree; very much; as, the word grew mightily.

In Scripture, most often of the operation of the Spirit of God upon men, or of the progress of His word.

From mighty, Saxon mihtig, from miht, might — the root also of may and main.

Key Scripture

Acts 19:20 — "So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed."

Judges 14:6 — "And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid, and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done."

Colossians 1:29 — "Whereunto I also labour, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily."

Jonah 3:8 — "But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto God: yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands."

Modern Corruption

Colossians 1:29 puts genuine human striving and God’s working in the same clause, which refutes both the quietist counsel to let go and let God and the activist assumption that ministry advances by human energy adequately applied.

expand to see more

Paul’s sentence is deliberately double: I also labour, striving according to his working, which worketh in me mightily. The labour is his, the striving is his — the word is agonizomenos, the language of the wrestling ring — and the energy that does the work is God’s. The Higher Life and Keswick tradition, with its counsel to cease from striving and let Christ live the life, has half the verse; the ministry-as-management approach, with its confidence that the right structures and sufficient effort produce growth, has the other half. Philippians 2:12-13 states the same doctrine in the same shape: work out your own salvation with fear and trembling. For it is God which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure. The for is the whole argument.

Judges 14:6 guards against a different error, the assumption that unusual power in a man’s ministry certifies his character. The Spirit came mightily on Samson while he was on his way to marry a Philistine woman against his parents’ counsel, and He came mightily on him again after worse. Gifts are given for the people, not as a testimonial to the man; Christ warned of those who would say have we not prophesied in thy name? and be told I never knew you. Acts 19:20 supplies the healthier measure. The thing Luke reports as growing mightily and prevailing is not a man’s influence but the word of God, and that is the only statistic the New Testament ever boasts in.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek ischuo (G2480), to be strong, to prevail; energeia (G1753), operative power, energy; dunamis (G1411), power; Hebrew tsalach (H6743), to rush upon, to prosper; chozqah (H2394), with force.

expand to see more

Greek ischuo (G2480) — to be strong, to prevail; so mightily grew the word of God and prevailed (Acts 19:20).

Greek energeia (G1753) — effectual working; his working, which worketh in me mightily (Colossians 1:29).

Greek agonizomai (G75) — to contend as in the games; the striving of the same verse.

Hebrew tsalach (H6743) — to rush, to break out upon; the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him (Judges 14:6).

Hebrew chozqah (H2394) — strength, force; cry mightily unto God (Jonah 3:8).

Usage

"So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed (Acts 19:20) — the word grows, the men are instruments."

"The Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him (Judges 14:6) — power given for the people, not as a testimonial to the man."

"His working, which worketh in me mightily (Colossians 1:29) — real striving, and the energy in it God’s."
